subject: QBR capacity requisition triage and prioritization
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: QBR capacity requisition triage and prioritization

Team —

QBR is three weeks out and finance wants a clean headcount plan for the next two quarters. I pulled together all active requisitions and split them into an initial triage sheet (attached). Please review and indicate whether each req should be: APPROVE (immediate hire), BACKFILL, DEFER (freeze until Q4), or CANCEL.

High-level asks:
- Review the "Critical" column first (SRE / Inference infra items).
- Call out any reqs you think are miscategorized (net-new vs backfill).
- If you need a quick cost note, flag it and Laura will coordinate with Finance.

Deadline: please mark your decisions in the sheet and reply with explicit approvals/no-go by end of day Thursday (2026-09-03). I will consolidate and send a final list to Finance and Recruiting on Friday morning for QBR prep.

Link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1QBR_reqs_2026
Attachment: QBR_reqs_2026-09.xlsx

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of People Strategy (interim)
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-02T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR capacity requisition triage and prioritization

Karthik —

Thanks for pulling this together. A couple quick notes from Talent/Finance perspective:
- We need clearer separation between BACKFILL and NET-NEW in the sheet. Right now some backfill rows are marked as net-new. This affects approval path.
- Finance has given a hard cap for incremental hires this quarter of 12 FTEs unless we have an exec-approved rationale. Can someone tag which reqs have a direct revenue/SLA impact?

I've attached the latest budget snapshot for context. If folks can highlight the top 8 hires they want to move forward with (and why), we can route the approvals faster.

Attachment: headcount_budget_snapshot.pdf

Laura Bennett
Director, Talent Partnering
Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-09-02T13:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR capacity requisition triage and prioritization

Karthik / Laura —

I reviewed the sheet and here are product's calls:
- APPROVE: Search Infra PM (REQ-2154) — this reduces time-to-value on our retrieval roadmap and impacts a number of revenue-related OKRs.
- APPROVE: Growth Eng (REQ-2221) — conversion improvements tied directly to Q4 expansion OKRs.
- BACKFILL: Senior UX Designer (REQ-2177) — role is a backfill; low ramp risk, schedule as low priority.
- DEFER: Junior UX Designer (REQ-2233) — deprioritize until pipeline shows improved conversion lift.

If Laura/Finance can sign off on the two approves, I'll sync with Recruiting to accelerate briefs and updated scorecards. Happy to present rationale in the QBR hiring slot.

Marissa Cole
VP, Product
Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-09-03T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR capacity requisition triage and prioritization

Team —

Heads up from Sales: we have two near-term expansion opportunities (ACME and NovaHealth) that materially depend on additional AE coverage and an implementation engineer for ACME (see HubSpot note: HubSpot-Deal-5764). If recruiting can't hit both AE hires immediately, we risk pushing ARR recognition out of Q4.

Proposed trade: move the Backend SWE req (REQ-2190) to DEFER and prioritize AE (REQ-2299) + Implementation Engineer (REQ-2310) for now. I'll own the executive rationale if we need to escalate to Finance.

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-09-04T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR capacity requisition triage and prioritization

Karthik / all —

From an engineering reliability lens: the SRE req (REQ-2138) should be classified as CRITICAL. Over the past two months we've had three incidents where lack of paging/on-call capacity increased mean time to recovery. Delaying this hire increases customer SLA risk and could trigger credits.

Cost note: The SRE hire (senior) has a blended ramp cost of ~ $220k fully burdened in year one. If Finance needs to reduce headcount this quarter, we should prioritize this role over low-impact product hires.

Attachment: sre-incident-brief.pdf

Stephanie Nguyen
Director of Engineering Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-05T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR capacity requisition triage and prioritization — consolidated decisions

Folks —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear asks. Summary of decisions and next steps (consolidated):

APPROVE (to Recruiting / Finance):
- REQ-2154 Search Infra PM (Product) — approved (Marissa)
- REQ-2221 Growth Engineer (Product) — approved (Marissa)
- REQ-2299 Account Executive (Sales) — approved (Vivek)
- REQ-2310 Implementation Engineer (Sales) — approved (Vivek)
- REQ-2138 Senior SRE (Engineering) — approved (Stephanie)

BACKFILL / SCHEDULING NOTES:
- REQ-2177 Senior UX Designer — backfill (schedule low-priority)

DEFER (freeze until Q4 unless exec exception):
- REQ-2190 Backend SWE — defer (proposed trade by Sales)
- REQ-2233 Junior UX Designer — defer

Action items:
- Laura: route these approvals to Finance for final sign-off against the 12-FTE cap and confirm funded start windows.
- Recruiting: prioritize briefs for the APPROVE list and start outreach; please confirm expected time-to-fill by EOD Friday.
- Marissa & Vivek: send a one-paragraph exec rationale for each APPROVE (tie to OKRs/revenue) so I can include in the QBR packet.

We will present this consolidated headcount plan in the QBR hiring segment. If Finance pushes back on the 12-FTE constraint, I will escalate to CTO/CEO with the attached evidence (sre-incident-brief + budget snapshot).

Thanks — great work moving quickly.

Karthik Iyer
Head of People Strategy (interim)
Redwood Inference
